input.quote: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
input.rationale: The grant in section 2(a) runs only to \"Client\", which is defined in the preamble as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone, so affiliates are not covered and there is no notice mechanism to add them; contractors are likewise unaddressed. Transferability also fails: section 15 bars assignment or transfer of rights without the other party's approval (with only a mutual affiliate exception) and nowhere permits transfer of the licence to a successor in a merger or acquisition. Both fallback elements therefore fail on material terms. We propose the shortest fallback cure: a new section 2(e) extending the licence to Client's affiliates on written notice and permitting a Client-only transfer to an M&A successor, without expanding TrueLink's assignment rights in section 15.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate coverage on written notice and Client-only licence transfer to an M&A successor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Interface licence to Client's affiliates on written notice and made it transferable to a Client successor in a merger or acquisition, which is our fallback licence-scope position. We left TrueLink's assignment rights in section 15 unchanged.

ops.text: Affiliates and Transfer. The license granted under section 2(a) extends to Client's affiliates upon written notice to TrueLink, and, notwithstanding section 15, Client may transfer the license to its successor in a merger or acquisition.
